title: Comparison of robotic-assisted and conventional implantation techniques in total knee arthroplasty using the VELYS™ Robotic-Assisted Solution
summary: Knee osteoarthritis is a common cause of pain and reduced mobility. When other treatments are no longer sufficient, an artificial knee joint can be implanted. However, not all patients are completely free of symptoms after surgery. This study investigates whether a robot-assisted surgical method for artificial knee joint implantation achieves at least similar results to the conventional manual method in routine clinical care. A third surgical method is also evaluated, in which the alignment of the artificial joint is planned differently. The study is a controlled, randomized investigation with three groups. A total of 300 adult patients are planned to be enrolled at one hospital. The main data collected include patient-reported function and quality of life, as well as mobility, radiographic measurements, duration of surgery, and length of hospital stay. No additional operations or additional radiographic examinations are performed solely for study purposes; the data are obtained from routine care and planned follow-up at 3, 12, and 24 months.
conditions: Primary knee osteoarthritis with indication for primary total knee arthroplasty

interventions.name:
Robotic-assisted mechanical alignment (RA-MA):
Primary total knee arthroplasty using the VELYS™ Robotic-Assisted Solution with mechanical alignment; operative strategy: tibia-first.

Robotic-assisted kinematic alignment (RA-KA):
Primary total knee arthroplasty using the VELYS™ Robotic-Assisted Solution with kinematic alignment; operative strategy: femur-first.

Manual mechanical alignment (MA):
Primary total knee arthroplasty using conventional manual instrumentation with mechanical alignment according to established standard of care; operative strategy: tibia-first.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Primary knee osteoarthritis with indication for primary total knee arthroplasty; capacity to consent and written informed consent; willingness and ability to complete patient-reported outcome assessments; availability of routine preoperative imaging.
Exclusion criteria:
Revision procedures, unicompartmental or simultaneous bilateral total knee arthroplasty; active infection, tumor disease, or recent fracture; inflammatory rheumatic systemic disease; pregnancy or breastfeeding; insufficient German language skills, inability to consent, or lack of follow-up reachability.
